name: Cleansing of the Infected
summary: In Darkshore, Tharnariun Treetender faces a hard choice over the infected thistle bears. His attempt to cure one has failed, and he asks you to kill the rabid beasts before they harm other creatures or spread the sickness.

sections.title: A Bitter Necessity
sections.body: Tharnariun Treetender has searched for a remedy to the sickness spreading through Darkshore's wildlife. He tried to cleanse a captured bear, but the thistle bears remain diseased and violent. Now he asks you to put them down. He fears they will maul other creatures and carry the sickness farther into the ancient woodlands.

sections.title: Containing the Wilds
sections.body: Tharnariun asks you to kill twenty rabid bears, though he knows it will not cure the plague. The killings buy time for Auberdine's defenders. Until anyone finds and severs the source of the forest's corruption, the settlement has no other way to hold back the aggressive herds and the danger they bring.

faq.q: Why does Tharnariun want the thistle bears killed instead of cured?
faq.answer: Tharnariun tried to cleanse a captured bear, but the cure failed and the beast died. Now the diseased bears threaten other creatures, so killing them is his last resort to slow the sickness's spread.

aliases: who gives cleansing of the infected
faq.answer: Tharnariun is a night elf caretaker in Auberdine. He studies the ailments affecting Darkshore's plants and animals and works to preserve nature's balance against the spreading corruption.

faq.q: Does slaying the rabid bears actually end the plague?
faq.answer: No. Tharnariun warns that killing the rabid bears will not stop the plague. It buys the forest and Auberdine's residents time by slowing the spread of infection and violence.

faq.q: What comes after Cleansing of the Infected?
faq.answer: After you report back, Tharnariun asks you to prepare for more bloodshed and offers Tharnariun's Hope, which continues the effort to deal with the blighted wildlife.

faq.q: Where are the rabid thistle bears found?
faq.answer: Rabid thistle bears roam the coastal and inland forests of central Darkshore, among the misty pines south and east of Auberdine.

faq.q: What caused the thistle bears to go rabid?
faq.answer: A mysterious taint sweeping through northern Kalimdor's woodlands has corrupted the bears, turning peaceful wildlife into frenzied, aggressive beasts that Tharnariun's attempted cure cannot heal.

angles.text: As a kaldorei, you bear the weight of ordering corrupted beasts killed. The sickness has reached deep into your ancestral homeland since the war.
As a druid, you may find Tharnariun's command especially painful. It is an act of mercy and care for the forest, not ordinary hunting.
As a hunter, you know that culling diseased predators can protect the wider ecology, even when the cause remains unknown.
